findings.title: Intro contradicts both frozen prose and its predicted series
findings.evidence: The rendered intro says, “No predictions or scoring here; every figure is computed from the LR cohort and spend tables.” Yet lines 627-629 explicitly describe the deal-synthesis values as “HARDCODED” and “Point-in-time literals,” lines 651-656 add another transcribed numeric conclusion, and lines 506-524 render a series named `Sum (predicted)` with a “predicted-vs-actual” subtitle. The authored venue repeats the categorical sentence at authored_pages/lr_historical/body.html:15-19 and the frozen numeric prose at body.html:50-129.
findings.failure_scenario: On every successful LR historical-page build, a reader sees the categorical provenance/no-predictions claim alongside client-specific numeric prose copied from source literals and a series explicitly labeled as predicted. The page therefore gives a false account of both how all visible numbers are produced and whether it contains a prediction.
findings.suggested_fix: In both venues, narrow the wording without changing the control clause—for example: “No forward projections or scoring here; the underlying historical observations are read from the LR cohort and spend tables, and the controls below affect only …”.

findings.title: Module docstring falsely denies its copied narrative literals
findings.evidence: The docstring says, “Every number is computed from the dev DB; nothing is a copied narrative literal.” The same module later says its synthesis is “HARDCODED,” “transcribed VERBATIM,” and made of “Point-in-time literals” at lines 627-629, with another transcribed numeric conclusion at lines 651-656.
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer or provenance reviewer trusts the module-level contract and treats all output as connection-derived, overlooking the frozen client measurements embedded in the source. It also incorrectly names the dev database even though `build` uses the supplied connection.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the categorical docstring sentence with an accurate split: chart/computed metrics read the named tables, while the synthesis and bottom-line prose contain separately sourced point-in-time literals.

overall_explanation: The four-table source enumeration, builder/authored parity, unchanged control clause, README consistency, and caption-golden rationale are all sound. The PR nevertheless preserves a reader-visible categorical sentence that the page itself contradicts through frozen numeric prose and an explicitly predicted series.
